veranderings.rede: 'Styg' already means 'go higher', so 'styg hoër' is doubled; the meaning stays the same without it.
'Stop' sounds like speech for a line of liquid that reaches a mark; 'eindig' is the more natural written word.

veranderings.voor: wat buite in die oopte die reën opvang
veranderings.na: wat die reën buite in die oopte opvang
veranderings.rede: A definite object usually comes before the adverbials of place in a subordinate clause, so this order reads more naturally.
'Ná' meaning 'after' takes the acute accent so that it is not read as 'na' (towards).

veranderings.blok: 'n Wind kry sy naam van waar hy vandaan kom
veranderings.na: Om die windrigting aan te dui, gebruik ons
veranderings.rede: 'Vir die windrigting gebruik ons' is wooden; an om-te clause says clearly what the four directions are used for.

veranderings.blok: Die windkous wys waarheen die wind waai
veranderings.rede: A tube's openings are its 'ente'; 'kante' can be read as its sides.

veranderings.blok: Die windkous wys waarheen die wind waai
veranderings.rede: Matches 'ente' in the previous sentence: the wind enters at the wide end of the tube.

veranderings.voor: en dit kom uit die weste
veranderings.na: en hy kom uit die weste
veranderings.rede: The lesson refers to the wind as 'hy' elsewhere ('waaruit hy waai'), so the pronoun should be consistent.

veranderings.na: kan meet hoeveel reën geval het
veranderings.rede: 'Hoeveel geval het' has no subject and reads incomplete; naming the rain makes the definition clear on its own.
